meta.title: Legacy Hive: Retire Now, Not on a Future Migration

views.label: Assess with UCX
views.note: UCX scans, maps grants, and generates upgrade notebooks without touching source objects.

views.label: Three upgrade methods
views.note: DEEP CLONE, external table recreation, or view recreation — chosen per table, not applied uniformly.

views.label: When a full upgrade can't happen yet
views.note: Federation queries Hive tables from UC-enabled clusters without forcing every table to upgrade before cutover.

cards.title: Two incidents this retires for good
items: Workspace-local Hive metastores don't share governance across workspaces — nothing here is portable
DBFS-backed managed tables are tied to a workspace; both the data and the metastore pointer must move
Deferring this moves the failure from planning time to cutover night, it doesn't avoid it

cards.title: Three methods, chosen per table
items: Hive managed (DBFS) upgrades via CREATE TABLE ... DEEP CLONE
Hive external upgrades via CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE at the new location
Hive views are recreated after their base tables exist

cards.title: Federation buys time, it doesn't replace upgrading
items: Hive metastore federation queries legacy tables from UC-enabled clusters
Migrate wave by wave rather than forcing one cutover for every table
Avoid creating new Hive assets in the source during the migration itself
